newsitem.title: UK: IFC signs $18 mln fertiliser deal in Pakistan.
newsitem.headline: IFC signs $18 mln fertiliser deal in Pakistan.

text.p: The International Finance Corporation (IFC) is to give $18 million to Engro Chemical Pakistan Ltd towards a $59 million project to modify a gas-based ammonia plant, it said in a statement on Tuesday.
IFC said it had signed an agreement with Engro on Monday.

Engro is Pakistan's second largest producer of urea fertiliser with a 21 percent share of the local market. The project will allow it to modify its plant in order to improve energy efficiency, increase capacity and reduce emissions.
It will allow Engro to conserve valuable natural gas used in the production of urea, which has a critical input in Pakistan's agriculture and the country's economy.

The project, which is to be completed by April 1998, will be the second financed for the company by the IFC in the last six years. The first project in 1991 allowed Engro to more than double production capacity from its orginal 268,000 metric tonnes per year (mt/yr) in the 1960s to 600,000 mt/yr.
IFC, part of the World Bank Group, is the largest multilateral source of equity and loan financing for private sector projects in developing countries.
Its financing of Engro's upgrading will consist of a loan of $9 million from its own account with a further $9 million coming from a syndicated loan from the accounts of participants.

Jean-Philippe Halphen, Director of IFC's Chemicals Petrochemicals and Fertiliser Department, said the project was a perfect combination of financial and economic viability, energy saving and environmental improvement. He added it should make a significant contribution to Engro's long-term competitiveness.
